newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to toughen crude oil export duty collection.
newsitem.headline: Russia to toughen crude oil export duty collection.

text.p: Russia plans to get tougher in collecting excise duties on crude oil exports, a senior State Customs Committee official said on Tuesday.

"The main task is to improve the collection of excise duties on crude oil exports that have been levied since August 1," said Vladimir Chuvayev, head of the committee's energy section, adding that a government decree on tighter collection measures would be signed soon.
Russia's crude oil export duty appears to contradict the terms of Moscow's agreement with the International Monetary Fund on a $10 billion, three-year loan.
Russia scrapped all energy export tariffs by July as part of the deal, but reintroduced a crude oil export levy last month.
"To some extent, the export duty contradicts the agreement with the IMF," Chuvayev said.

IMF officials could not be reached for immediate comment, but mission representatives in Moscow have said the reintroduced levy is a tax, not a tariff, and does not seem to contradict the terms of the agreement.

Duties on crude oil exports varying from 51,649 roubles to 82,536 roubles per tonne were introduced in line with a government decree aimed at raising federal budget revenues -- a goal advocated by the fund.
Exports of refined oil products are not dutiable.

Russia temporarily collected an excise duty of 70,000 roubles for each tonne of oil sold -- a form of levy the IMF supports -- but Chuvayev said that the sales tax had been scrapped when the new export levy came into place in August.
He said that under the new rules of enforced collection, late-paying companies would be subject to fines equal to 0.3 percent of the sum due for each day late after a certain date.
"If payments are delayed for 1-1/2 months or more, the customs committee could limit the export operations of the debtor or oblige him to pay duties in advance," he said.
Trading companies which export crude oil for refining in other countries and then import and sell the refined products in Russia must pay the duty.
Russian re-exports of crude oil purchased in other countries are not dutiable, he said.
Over 100 companies, including those producing and selling oil, are currently paying excise duties.
Trading companies which do not produce oil themselves will continue to pay the maximum export duty of 82,536 roubles per tonne, Chuvayev said.
About 20 oil producers pay the minimum duty of 51,649 roubles, but some companies from southern Russia and the Northern Caucasus are exempt.
"These export duties are a new phenomenon for Russia and their payment rules need to be clarified," Chuvayev said.
"The procedure will be a real headache for customs officers".
